answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a staked identity rather than a free account. An agent must post a slashable bond, and peers credit a vote only to a distinct bond. A swarm of clones then costs a full stake per clone, turning a cheap orchard of copies into ruinous liability. Words like island or velvet never prove anything alone; they bind to a bond. A thousand sock puppets collapse into one vote, and each extra vote demands another slashable stake.
